# corrections.txt
#
# Applied in file order, once each, case-insensitively.
# Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.
#
# Two rule forms:
#   literal => replacement        whole-word match, case adapted to the source
#   regex: PATTERN => replacement PATTERN is a Go regexp, matched case-insensitively
#
# IMPORTANT: only add a literal rule for a string that is NEVER correct.
# "lessons => lessens" would break every legitimate use of "lessons".
# For cases like that, use a regex rule with surrounding context.

# --- Observed on L'Abri recordings ---

sensorous => censorious
termith => termeth

# "at L'Abri" rendered as "at lab" by all models tested.
# Hazard: "at lab meeting" would be wrongly rewritten. Acceptable for this
# corpus; use a regex rule with context if it ever misfires.
at lab => at L'Abri

# "Pontus" in 1 Peter 1:1, misheard as "Pontius" by every model tested.
# Hazard: Pontius Pilate. Safe while the corpus is lecture material.
Pontius => Pontus

# --- Context-sensitive cases, shown for reference ---

# "contracts and lessons" should be "contracts and lessens".
# Cannot be a literal rule: "lessons" is a common correct word.
regex: (contracts? and )lessons\b => ${1}lessens

# --- Add speaker and place names as you find them ---
# Jamie Kipiak => Jamie Kipiak
